conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__HIV (clinical.explanation: Women with HIV are at increased risk of HPV-related cervical disease, so annual cervical smears are recommended (more frequent than the general population). Other holistic care includes vaccinations, cardiovascular risk management and bone/renal monitoring.

conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__HIV (clinical.question: A baby is born to an HIV-positive mother whose viral load was <50 copies/mL throughout. What neonatal prophylaxis is most appropriate?
options: Combination zidovudine + lamivudine + nevirapine for 4 weeks
A single dose of nevirapine only
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__HIV (clinical.answer: Zidovudine monotherapy for 2–4 weeks
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__HIV (clinical.explanation: For a low-risk infant (maternal viral load <50), neonatal post-exposure prophylaxis is zidovudine monotherapy for 2–4 weeks. High-risk infants (higher maternal load) receive combination prophylaxis (zidovudine + lamivudine + nevirapine) for 4 weeks.

conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__HIV (clinical.question: Which statement about HIV diagnostic testing is correct?
options: A 4th-generation test detects antibody and p24 antigen and is positive from around 4 weeks
HIV can be reliably excluded 3 days after exposure
Viral load is the initial screening test of choice
CD4 count is used to diagnose HIV
Only a lymph node biopsy can confirm HIV
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__HIV (clinical.answer: A 4th-generation test detects antibody and p24 antigen and is positive from around 4 weeks
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__HIV (clinical.explanation: The standard diagnostic is a 4th-generation lab test detecting HIV antibody plus p24 antigen, which becomes positive from about 4 weeks (repeat per window period if early). CD4 count and viral load are used for staging/monitoring, not diagnosis, and a very early test after exposure cannot exclude infection.

conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__HIV (clinical.question: A HIV-positive man with a CD4 of 180 develops a dry cough and marked breathlessness on exertion with desaturation on walking, and a clear-ish chest X-ray. What is the most likely diagnosis?
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__HIV (clinical.answer: Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia (PCP)
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__HIV (clinical.explanation: A subacute dry cough with exertional breathlessness and desaturation at a CD4 <200, often with a relatively unremarkable early chest X-ray, is classic for Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia. Treatment (and prophylaxis) is with co-trimoxazole; steroids are added if hypoxic.

conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__HIV (clinical.question: A healthcare worker sustains a needlestick injury from a patient known to be HIV-positive. How soon should post-exposure prophylaxis ideally be started?
options: As soon as possible and within 72 hours
Only after confirmatory HIV testing at 6 weeks
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__HIV (clinical.answer: As soon as possible and within 72 hours
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__HIV (clinical.explanation: Occupational PEP should be started as soon as possible and within 72 hours of exposure (the sooner the better; it is considered ineffective after 72 hours). The regimen is Truvada + raltegravir (or dolutegravir) for 28 days, with baseline and follow-up HIV testing.

conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__HIV (clinical.question: A patient prefers not to take daily HIV tablets. Which modern ART option could be offered?
options: A single annual infusion of tenofovir
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__HIV (clinical.answer: Long-acting injectable cabotegravir + rilpivirine given 2-monthly
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__HIV (clinical.explanation: Long-acting injectable ART with cabotegravir + rilpivirine, given every 2 months, is an option for people who prefer not to take daily oral therapy, provided they are suitable and virologically suppressed. PrEP is for HIV-negative people, not treatment.

conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__HIV (clinical.question: Which of the following best distinguishes PrEP from PEP?
options: PrEP is taken after exposure; PEP is taken before
PrEP is taken by HIV-negative people to prevent acquisition (daily/event-based); PEP is a 28-day course started within 72 hours after a specific exposure
They are identical regimens with different names
PrEP is for HIV-positive people; PEP is for HIV-negative people
PEP is a lifelong daily tablet
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__HIV (clinical.answer: PrEP is taken by HIV-negative people to prevent acquisition (daily/event-based); PEP is a 28-day course started within 72 hours after a specific exposure
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__HIV (clinical.explanation: PrEP (tenofovir/emtricitabine, daily or event-based) is taken by HIV-negative people at ongoing risk to prevent acquisition. PEP is started AFTER a specific potential exposure, within 72 hours, as a 28-day course (Truvada + raltegravir) to prevent seroconversion.

conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__HIV (clinical.question: A pregnant woman with HIV presents in labour and her most recent viral load is >1000 copies/mL. In addition to planning delivery, what intrapartum intervention is indicated?
options: Immediate breastfeeding to boost infant immunity
A single dose of nevirapine to the mother only
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__HIV (clinical.answer: IV zidovudine during labour/delivery
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__HIV (clinical.explanation: With an unknown or high viral load (>1000 copies/mL), IV zidovudine is given during labour to reduce vertical transmission, alongside a pre-labour caesarean. The neonate would then receive combination post-exposure prophylaxis as a high-risk infant.

conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__HIV (clinical.question: An HIV-positive mother who is fully suppressed on ART wishes to breastfeed. What is the correct UK advice?
options: Breastfeeding is absolutely forbidden in all circumstances
The UK default is formula feeding, but if she is fully suppressed on ART and chooses to breastfeed, this can be supported with close monitoring
She should breastfeed as it carries no risk
She must stop ART while breastfeeding
Mixed feeding is the safest option
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__HIV (clinical.answer: The UK default is formula feeding, but if she is fully suppressed on ART and chooses to breastfeed, this can be supported with close monitoring
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__HIV (clinical.explanation: The UK default remains formula feeding to eliminate transmission risk. However, BHIVA now supports women who are fully virologically suppressed on ART and choose to breastfeed, with close monitoring, recognising individual circumstances. Mixed feeding is discouraged.

conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__HIV (clinical.question: Which infection can occur at any CD4 count and is the commonest HIV-associated opportunistic infection globally?
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__HIV (clinical.answer: Tuberculosis
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__HIV (clinical.explanation: Tuberculosis can occur at any CD4 count and is the commonest HIV-associated opportunistic infection worldwide. Others such as CMV (CD4 <50), PCP (CD4 <200) and cryptococcal meningitis tend to occur at lower CD4 counts.

conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__HIV (clinical.question: A patient's HIV viral load is reported as 'undetectable (<50 copies/mL)' after starting ART. What does this indicate?
options: The virus has been eradicated and ART can stop
Effective viral suppression — the treatment goal — but ART must continue lifelong
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__HIV (clinical.answer: Effective viral suppression — the treatment goal — but ART must continue lifelong
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__HIV (clinical.explanation: An undetectable viral load (<50 copies/mL) indicates effective suppression — the goal of ART — leading to immune recovery and U=U. However, HIV is not eradicated (it persists in reservoirs), so ART must be continued lifelong; stopping would allow viral rebound.

conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__HIV (clinical.question: A patient with advanced HIV develops progressive focal neurological signs and a ring-enhancing brain lesion on imaging. Which AIDS-associated condition is the most likely cause?
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__HIV (clinical.answer: Cerebral toxoplasmosis
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__HIV (clinical.explanation: In advanced HIV, cerebral toxoplasmosis classically causes focal neurological deficits with ring-enhancing lesions on brain imaging. Primary CNS lymphoma (EBV-related) is the main differential; empirical anti-toxoplasma treatment with follow-up imaging is often used to distinguish them.

conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Gonorrhoea.question: A 26-year-old man presents with dysuria and a profuse, purulent green urethral discharge. A urethral Gram stain shows gram-negative intracellular diplococci. What is the most likely diagnosis and the correct first-line treatment when sensitivities are not yet known?
options: Chlamydia — doxycycline 100 mg BD for 7 days
Gonorrhoea — ceftriaxone 1 g IM single dose (monotherapy)
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Gonorrhoea.answer: Gonorrhoea — ceftriaxone 1 g IM single dose (monotherapy)
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Gonorrhoea.explanation: Gram-negative intracellular diplococci with purulent discharge indicate gonorrhoea. When sensitivities are unknown, first-line is ceftriaxone 1 g IM monotherapy. Azithromycin has been dropped (rising resistance), and empirical ciprofloxacin is not used unless the isolate is known to be sensitive.

conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Gonorrhoea.question: When managing gonorrhoea, which investigation is essential BEFORE giving treatment and distinguishes its work-up from chlamydia?
options: A test of cure by NAAT
A charcoal swab for culture and sensitivities
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Gonorrhoea.answer: A charcoal swab for culture and sensitivities
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Gonorrhoea.explanation: Because of high and rising gonococcal resistance, a charcoal swab for culture and sensitivities must be taken before treatment (NAAT confirms the organism but only culture gives sensitivities). This pre-treatment culture step is a key difference from chlamydia management.

conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Gonorrhoea.question: A woman is treated for gonorrhoea with ceftriaxone. Regarding a test of cure, what is the correct advice?
options: A test of cure is not needed as ceftriaxone is highly effective
A test of cure is recommended for all gonorrhoea cases because of resistance
A test of cure is only needed if she becomes pregnant
Repeat the NAAT at 24 hours to confirm cure
A test of cure is only needed for men
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Gonorrhoea.answer: A test of cure is recommended for all gonorrhoea cases because of resistance
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Gonorrhoea.explanation: Unlike chlamydia (where TOC is not routine), a test of cure is recommended for ALL gonorrhoea cases because of antimicrobial resistance — especially after pharyngeal infection or if symptoms persist. Timing avoids false positives from dead organisms (culture ≥72 h; RNA NAAT ≥7 d; DNA NAAT ≥14 d).

conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Gonorrhoea.question: Which statement about the tissue tropism of Neisseria gonorrhoeae is correct?
options: It preferentially infects squamous vaginal epithelium
It infects mucous membranes lined by columnar epithelium — endocervix, urethra, rectum, conjunctiva and pharynx
It cannot infect the pharynx or rectum
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Gonorrhoea.answer: It infects mucous membranes lined by columnar epithelium — endocervix, urethra, rectum, conjunctiva and pharynx
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Gonorrhoea.explanation: Gonorrhoea infects columnar epithelium — endocervix, urethra, rectum, conjunctiva and pharynx — but not the squamous vaginal epithelium. This tropism explains why endocervical/urethral/rectal/pharyngeal sites are affected and why testing at all sites of exposure matters.

conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Gonorrhoea.question: A neonate develops a profuse purulent conjunctivitis with marked lid swelling within the first 48 hours of life, born vaginally to an untreated mother. What is the most concerning diagnosis and why is it urgent?
options: Gonococcal ophthalmia neonatorum — can cause corneal perforation and blindness, and is associated with sepsis
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Gonorrhoea.answer: Gonococcal ophthalmia neonatorum — can cause corneal perforation and blindness, and is associated with sepsis
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Gonorrhoea.explanation: Early (first few days), profuse, purulent neonatal conjunctivitis suggests gonococcal ophthalmia neonatorum — a medical emergency that can cause corneal perforation and blindness and is associated with sepsis, requiring urgent treatment. Chlamydial ophthalmia tends to present later (around 5–14 days) and is generally less aggressive.

conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Gonorrhoea.question: A young woman presents with fever, painful migratory joint pains, tenosynovitis of the wrists, and scattered pustular skin lesions. She recently had unprotected sex. What is the most likely diagnosis?
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Gonorrhoea.explanation: The triad of dermatitis (pustular/haemorrhagic lesions), migratory polyarthritis/arthralgia and tenosynovitis in a sexually active young person is classic for disseminated gonococcal infection (DGI), from haematogenous spread. It may progress to purulent septic arthritis and, rarely, endocarditis/meningitis.

conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Gonorrhoea.question: A patient's gonorrhoea culture confirms the isolate is ciprofloxacin-sensitive. Which treatment option does this make available, and what caution applies?
options: Ciprofloxacin 500 mg PO single dose, avoiding an injection — with the MHRA fluoroquinolone caution
Azithromycin 1 g single dose is preferred
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Gonorrhoea.answer: Ciprofloxacin 500 mg PO single dose, avoiding an injection — with the MHRA fluoroquinolone caution
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Gonorrhoea.explanation: When culture confirms ciprofloxacin sensitivity, oral ciprofloxacin 500 mg single dose can be used, avoiding an intramuscular injection. This is only appropriate when susceptibility is confirmed, and MHRA fluoroquinolone cautions (tendon/neuro/QT) apply. Empirically (sensitivity unknown) the drug of choice remains ceftriaxone.

conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Gonorrhoea.question: Why has azithromycin been dropped from the standard empirical gonorrhoea regimen?
options: It caused too many allergic reactions
Because of rising azithromycin resistance; the higher-dose ceftriaxone monotherapy covers reduced-susceptibility strains and dropping azithromycin reduces resistance pressure
It is ineffective against chlamydia coinfection
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Gonorrhoea.answer: Because of rising azithromycin resistance; the higher-dose ceftriaxone monotherapy covers reduced-susceptibility strains and dropping azithromycin reduces resistance pressure
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Gonorrhoea.explanation: The dual regimen (ceftriaxone + azithromycin) was replaced by ceftriaxone 1 g IM monotherapy because of rising azithromycin resistance. The higher ceftriaxone dose covers strains with reduced cephalosporin susceptibility, and removing azithromycin reduces selection pressure for resistance.

conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Gonorrhoea.question: A man diagnosed with gonorrhoea is also found to have chlamydia on his STI screen. How should this be managed?
options: Treat only the gonorrhoea, as it is more serious
Treat gonorrhoea specifically (ceftriaxone) AND treat the chlamydia (doxycycline); coinfection is common
A single dose of azithromycin will cover both
No treatment until sensitivities for both return
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Gonorrhoea.answer: Treat gonorrhoea specifically (ceftriaxone) AND treat the chlamydia (doxycycline); coinfection is common
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Gonorrhoea.explanation: Chlamydia coinfection is common, so both are treated — gonorrhoea specifically with ceftriaxone 1 g IM and chlamydia with doxycycline 100 mg BD for 7 days. A full STI screen and GUM referral for partner notification are also standard.

conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Gonorrhoea.question: Which feature most reliably distinguishes typical gonorrhoea from typical chlamydia at presentation?
options: Gonorrhoea is usually asymptomatic; chlamydia is usually symptomatic
Gonorrhoea is more often symptomatic with a purulent green/yellow discharge; chlamydia is largely asymptomatic
Chlamydia causes purulent green discharge; gonorrhoea causes none
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Gonorrhoea.answer: Gonorrhoea is more often symptomatic with a purulent green/yellow discharge; chlamydia is largely asymptomatic
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Gonorrhoea.explanation: Gonorrhoea is more often symptomatic and classically produces a purulent green/yellow discharge with dysuria, whereas chlamydia is largely asymptomatic and often detected on screening. (However, gonococcal pharyngeal and rectal infections are frequently silent.)

conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Gonorrhoea.question: A GUM clinic wants to detect gonorrhoea at all potential sites in an MSM patient who reports oral and anal sex. Which testing approach is correct?
options: NAAT at urethral/urine plus rectal and pharyngeal swabs, with charcoal swabs for culture where positive/symptomatic
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Gonorrhoea.answer: NAAT at urethral/urine plus rectal and pharyngeal swabs, with charcoal swabs for culture where positive/symptomatic
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Gonorrhoea.explanation: Because gonorrhoea infects columnar epithelium at multiple sites (often silently in the pharynx and rectum), NAAT should be performed at all sites of exposure — urethral/urine plus rectal and pharyngeal swabs — with charcoal culture swabs taken for sensitivities. Testing only one site would miss extragenital infection.

conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Gonorrhoea.question: A patient treated for pharyngeal gonorrhoea returns for follow-up. Why is a test of cure particularly important for this site?
options: Pharyngeal infection is always symptomatic so cure is obvious
Pharyngeal gonorrhoea is harder to eradicate and often asymptomatic, and resistance is a concern, so TOC is especially important
TOC is never needed for pharyngeal infection
A test of cure is only for genital sites
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Gonorrhoea.answer: Pharyngeal gonorrhoea is harder to eradicate and often asymptomatic, and resistance is a concern, so TOC is especially important
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Gonorrhoea.explanation: Pharyngeal gonorrhoea is more difficult to eradicate and is often asymptomatic, and with rising resistance a test of cure is recommended for all cases but especially after pharyngeal infection to confirm eradication.

conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Gonorrhoea.question: A 30-year-old woman with gonococcal cervicitis develops lower abdominal pain, cervical motion tenderness and fever. What complication has developed and what is the long-term risk?
options: Pelvic inflammatory disease — risk of infertility and ectopic pregnancy
Ovarian torsion — risk of loss of ovary
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Gonorrhoea.answer: Pelvic inflammatory disease — risk of infertility and ectopic pregnancy
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Gonorrhoea.explanation: Ascending gonococcal infection causes pelvic inflammatory disease (lower abdominal pain, cervical motion tenderness, fever), which risks tubal damage leading to infertility and ectopic pregnancy. This requires prompt broad empirical PID treatment.

conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Gonorrhoea.question: A symptomatic man's urethral Gram stain shows gram-negative intracellular diplococci. What does this allow, and what must still be done?
options: A rapid presumptive diagnosis of gonorrhoea allowing prompt treatment, but a charcoal swab for culture/sensitivities should still be taken before treating
Confirmation that there is no chlamydia coinfection
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Gonorrhoea.answer: A rapid presumptive diagnosis of gonorrhoea allowing prompt treatment, but a charcoal swab for culture/sensitivities should still be taken before treating
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Gonorrhoea.explanation: A urethral Gram stain showing gram-negative intracellular diplococci gives a rapid presumptive diagnosis in symptomatic men, allowing prompt ceftriaxone treatment. A charcoal swab for culture and sensitivities should still be taken beforehand because of resistance, and chlamydia coinfection should be tested for and treated.

conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Gonorrhoea.question: Which of the following best explains why antimicrobial stewardship is emphasised so heavily in gonorrhoea?
options: Ceftriaxone is the last reliable first-line agent and ceftriaxone-resistant strains are already emerging
Antibiotics have no effect on gonorrhoea
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Gonorrhoea.answer: Ceftriaxone is the last reliable first-line agent and ceftriaxone-resistant strains are already emerging
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Gonorrhoea.explanation: Gonococci have sequentially developed resistance to penicillins, tetracyclines and quinolones, leaving ceftriaxone as the last reliable first-line agent — and resistant strains are already emerging. This drives the stewardship measures: higher-dose monotherapy, mandatory culture with sensitivities, and test of cure for all cases.

conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Gonorrhoea.question: A 22-year-old woman is diagnosed with gonorrhoea and asks when she can resume sexual activity. What is the correct advice?
options: No sex until treatment is complete and a test of cure has been done (at least 7 days), and until partners are treated
There are no restrictions once symptoms improve
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Gonorrhoea.answer: No sex until treatment is complete and a test of cure has been done (at least 7 days), and until partners are treated
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Gonorrhoea.explanation: Advise no sex until treatment is complete and the test of cure is done (minimum 7 days) and until partners have been treated, to prevent reinfection and onward transmission. GUM referral for partner notification and testing for other STIs are also part of management.

conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Gonorrhoea.question: A patient with a severe cephalosporin allergy is diagnosed with gonorrhoea, and sensitivities are not yet available. What is the most appropriate approach?
options: Seek specialist GUM advice for an alternative regimen guided by culture sensitivities, as first-line ceftriaxone cannot be used
Give azithromycin 1 g alone as monotherapy
Withhold all treatment until the patient can tolerate ceftriaxone
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Gonorrhoea.answer: Seek specialist GUM advice for an alternative regimen guided by culture sensitivities, as first-line ceftriaxone cannot be used
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Gonorrhoea.explanation: With a genuine severe cephalosporin allergy, first-line ceftriaxone cannot be given, so specialist GUM advice is needed and treatment is guided by culture and sensitivities (e.g. ciprofloxacin if the isolate is sensitive, or other second-line options). Azithromycin or doxycycline monotherapy is inadequate for gonorrhoea given resistance.

conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Gonorrhoea.question: Which of the following is a recognised local complication of gonorrhoea in men?
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Gonorrhoea.explanation: In men, gonorrhoea can cause epididymo-orchitis, prostatitis and urethral strictures. In women it can cause PID leading to infertility and ectopic pregnancy. Disseminated infection and increased HIV transmission are additional important complications.

conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Epididymo-orc.question: A 17-year-old boy presents with sudden, severe left testicular pain for 2 hours with vomiting. The testis is high-riding with a horizontal lie and the cremasteric reflex is absent. There are no urinary symptoms. What is the most appropriate immediate management?
options: Empirical ceftriaxone and doxycycline for epididymo-orchitis
Urgent scrotal Doppler ultrasound before any intervention
Reassurance and analgesia with GP follow-up
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Epididymo-orc.explanation: This is testicular torsion (sudden severe pain, vomiting, high-riding horizontal testis, absent cremasteric reflex, young age). Torsion is a surgical emergency with a ~6-hour salvage window, so the correct action is urgent surgical exploration — NOT waiting for an ultrasound. Imaging must not delay exploration when torsion is clinically suspected.

conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Epididymo-orc.question: A 24-year-old sexually active man has a 2-day history of gradually worsening right scrotal pain and swelling, with urethral discharge and dysuria. The cremasteric reflex is present. Torsion is felt to be excluded. What is the most likely causative organism group?
options: Enteric organisms such as E. coli
Sexually transmitted organisms — Chlamydia trachomatis and Neisseria gonorrhoeae
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Epididymo-orc.answer: Sexually transmitted organisms — Chlamydia trachomatis and Neisseria gonorrhoeae
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Epididymo-orc.explanation: In a younger (<35), sexually active man with urethral discharge, the likely cause is sexually transmitted — chlamydia and gonorrhoea. Enteric organisms (E. coli) predominate in older, low-risk men with urinary symptoms or instrumentation. The gradual onset, present cremasteric reflex and urethral symptoms fit epididymo-orchitis rather than torsion.

conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Epididymo-orc.question: A 24-year-old man with suspected STI-related epididymo-orchitis needs empirical treatment before culture results. According to current BASHH guidance, what is the correct regimen?
options: Ceftriaxone 500 mg IM + doxycycline 100 mg BD for 14 days
Ceftriaxone 1 g IM single dose + doxycycline 100 mg PO BD for 10–14 days
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Epididymo-orc.answer: Ceftriaxone 1 g IM single dose + doxycycline 100 mg PO BD for 10–14 days
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Epididymo-orc.explanation: For an STI cause, treat empirically with ceftriaxone 1 g IM (single dose) plus doxycycline 100 mg BD for 10–14 days. The currency point is that the dose is now 1 g (BASHH 2020, aligned with the gonorrhoea guideline for reduced-susceptibility strains), not the older 500 mg. Ofloxacin alone would be for an enteric cause.

conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Epididymo-orc.question: A 68-year-old man with benign prostatic hyperplasia and a recent urinary catheter develops gradual-onset right scrotal pain with dysuria and positive nitrites on dipstick. Torsion is excluded. What is the most appropriate empirical treatment?
options: Ceftriaxone 1 g IM + doxycycline for 14 days
Ofloxacin 200 mg PO BD for 14 days (covering enteric organisms)
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Epididymo-orc.answer: Ofloxacin 200 mg PO BD for 14 days (covering enteric organisms)
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Epididymo-orc.explanation: In an older, low-sexual-risk man with urinary symptoms and instrumentation, the cause is enteric (E. coli), so a quinolone such as ofloxacin 200 mg BD for 14 days (or levofloxacin) is appropriate, with MHRA fluoroquinolone cautions noted. STI-directed ceftriaxone + doxycycline is for younger, sexually active men.

conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Epididymo-orc.question: Which examination finding is most reassuring AGAINST testicular torsion but must never be used alone to exclude it?
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Epididymo-orc.explanation: A present cremasteric reflex favours epididymo-orchitis over torsion (in which it is typically absent). However, no single sign — including Prehn's sign or the cremasteric reflex — is reliable enough to exclude torsion; if torsion cannot be confidently excluded, urgent surgical exploration is required.

conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Epididymo-orc.question: A man treated empirically for STI-related epididymo-orchitis asks what else is required beyond his antibiotics. What is the most appropriate advice?
options: No further action once antibiotics are prescribed
No sex until treatment is complete, plus GUM referral for a full STI screen and partner notification
A test of cure at 48 hours
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Epididymo-orc.answer: No sex until treatment is complete, plus GUM referral for a full STI screen and partner notification
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Epididymo-orc.explanation: When the cause is an STI, management includes advising no sex until treatment is complete and referral to GUM for a full STI screen and partner notification, in addition to the antibiotics and supportive measures. This prevents onward transmission and reinfection.

conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Epididymo-orc.question: A 30-year-old man reports insertive anal sex and now has epididymo-orchitis. Given a mixed STI and enteric risk, what is the most appropriate empirical treatment?
options: Ceftriaxone 1 g IM + ofloxacin 200 mg BD for 14 days
Ceftriaxone 500 mg IM single dose only
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Epididymo-orc.answer: Ceftriaxone 1 g IM + ofloxacin 200 mg BD for 14 days
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Epididymo-orc.explanation: With mixed STI and enteric risk (e.g. insertive anal sex), cover both by combining ceftriaxone 1 g IM (for gonorrhoea) with ofloxacin 200 mg BD for 14 days (for chlamydia and enteric organisms). Single-agent therapy would leave one likely pathogen group untreated.

conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Epididymo-orc.question: A scrotal Doppler ultrasound is being considered in a young man with acute scrotal pain in whom torsion cannot be clinically excluded. What is the correct approach?
options: Perform the ultrasound first and act on the result
Proceed to urgent surgical exploration without delaying for imaging
Discharge with oral antibiotics and outpatient scan
Give analgesia and reassess in the morning
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Epididymo-orc.answer: Proceed to urgent surgical exploration without delaying for imaging
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Epididymo-orc.explanation: If torsion cannot be excluded clinically, urgent surgical exploration is mandatory and must NOT be delayed for imaging — the testis must be salvaged within ~6 hours. Doppler ultrasound can support a diagnosis of epididymo-orchitis but has no role if it would delay exploration for suspected torsion.

conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Epididymo-orc.question: A 22-year-old man is found on urethral Gram stain to have gram-negative intracellular diplococci alongside his epididymo-orchitis. Which organism does this indicate and how does it affect treatment?
options: Neisseria gonorrhoeae — ensure ceftriaxone is included
E. coli — treat with ofloxacin alone
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Epididymo-orc.answer: Neisseria gonorrhoeae — ensure ceftriaxone is included
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Epididymo-orc.explanation: Gram-negative intracellular diplococci indicate Neisseria gonorrhoeae, so treatment must include ceftriaxone 1 g IM (plus doxycycline to cover co-existing chlamydia). This is why the STI regimen is dual therapy rather than doxycycline alone.

conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Epididymo-orc.question: A previously well 19-year-old presents with bilateral testicular pain and swelling a few days after parotid gland swelling and fever. What is the most likely cause of his orchitis?
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Epididymo-orc.explanation: Orchitis following parotitis (parotid swelling) and fever is classic mumps orchitis — a non-STI viral cause, often bilateral, which can impair fertility. Management is supportive. It should be distinguished from bacterial epididymo-orchitis and from torsion.

conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Epididymo-orc.question: A 40-year-old man has a persistent, painless testicular mass that does not settle after treatment for presumed epididymo-orchitis. What is the key red-flag diagnosis to exclude?
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Epididymo-orc.explanation: A persistent, painless testicular mass is a red flag for testicular tumour, which must be excluded (ultrasound + tumour markers). Epididymo-orchitis that fails to settle should prompt re-imaging to look for an abscess or an underlying tumour.

conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Epididymo-orc.question: Which of the following best distinguishes the typical ONSET of epididymo-orchitis from testicular torsion?
options: Epididymo-orchitis is sudden and severe; torsion is gradual
Epididymo-orchitis develops more gradually over hours to days; torsion is sudden and severe
Both have an identical instantaneous onset
Torsion always develops over several days
Onset is never helpful in distinguishing them
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Epididymo-orc.answer: Epididymo-orchitis develops more gradually over hours to days; torsion is sudden and severe
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Epididymo-orc.explanation: Epididymo-orchitis typically develops more gradually over hours to days, often with urinary/urethral symptoms and fever, whereas torsion is characteristically sudden and severe (often <6 hours) with vomiting. Onset helps but does not replace the need to exclude torsion in any acute scrotum.

conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Epididymo-orc.question: A man with STI-related epididymo-orchitis is being treated. Which complication is most associated with bilateral disease?
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Epididymo-orc.explanation: Reduced fertility is a recognised complication, particularly with bilateral epididymo-orchitis (as also seen with bilateral mumps orchitis). Other complications include abscess formation, testicular infarction/atrophy, hydrocele/pyocele and chronic scrotal pain.

conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Epididymo-orc.question: A 26-year-old man with epididymo-orchitis is treated with ofloxacin because of a possible enteric cause. What important prescribing caution applies to this drug class?
options: It is completely free of significant side effects
Fluoroquinolones carry MHRA cautions regarding tendon, neurological and QT effects
It must be avoided in all men over 30
It is contraindicated with scrotal support
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Epididymo-orc.answer: Fluoroquinolones carry MHRA cautions regarding tendon, neurological and QT effects
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Epididymo-orc.explanation: Fluoroquinolones (ofloxacin, levofloxacin) carry MHRA cautions regarding tendon damage/rupture, neurological effects and QT prolongation, so they should be used with appropriate caution and counselling. They remain a standard choice for the enteric cause of epididymo-orchitis.

conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Epididymo-orc.question: A young man presents with an acute scrotum. Which single principle should govern the initial approach regardless of the eventual diagnosis?
options: Start antibiotics immediately and review in a week
Exclude testicular torsion first, proceeding to urgent exploration if it cannot be excluded clinically
Arrange an outpatient ultrasound and analgesia
Reassure, as most acute scrotal pain is benign
Perform an STI screen before anything else
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Epididymo-orc.answer: Exclude testicular torsion first, proceeding to urgent exploration if it cannot be excluded clinically
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Epididymo-orc.explanation: In any acute scrotum, testicular torsion must be excluded first because it is a time-critical surgical emergency (salvage <6 hours). If torsion cannot be excluded clinically, proceed to urgent surgical exploration without delaying for imaging — only once torsion is excluded do you work up and treat epididymo-orchitis by likely organism.

conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Epididymo-orc.question: A 33-year-old man with epididymo-orchitis of uncertain cause is started on treatment but his symptoms are not settling after several days. What is the most appropriate next step?
options: Continue the same treatment for 3 months
Re-image the scrotum to look for an abscess or underlying tumour
Reassure and discharge with no follow-up
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Epididymo-orc.answer: Re-image the scrotum to look for an abscess or underlying tumour
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Epididymo-orc.explanation: Failure to settle warrants re-imaging (scrotal ultrasound) to look for complications such as an abscess or an underlying testicular tumour, and to reconsider the diagnosis/organism. Follow-up is an explicit part of management; premature surgery or simply continuing ineffective treatment is inappropriate.

conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Chlamydia.question: A 21-year-old sexually active woman attends for a routine check and has no symptoms. According to the National Chlamydia Screening Programme, what is the most appropriate action?
options: No screening is needed as she is asymptomatic
Offer chlamydia screening (annually or on change of partner) with a self-taken vulvovaginal swab
Screen only if she requests it
Perform an endocervical swab under direct vision only
Screen for chlamydia with a blood test
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Chlamydia.answer: Offer chlamydia screening (annually or on change of partner) with a self-taken vulvovaginal swab
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Chlamydia.explanation: The NCSP recommends screening every sexually active person under 25 annually or on change of partner, precisely because most infections are asymptomatic. In women the first-line NAAT specimen is a vulvovaginal swab, which can be self-taken. Chlamydia is diagnosed by NAAT, not serology.

conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Chlamydia.question: A 23-year-old man has urethral discomfort and a positive first-catch urine NAAT for Chlamydia trachomatis. He has no allergies and is not on other medication. What is the first-line treatment?
options: Doxycycline 100 mg twice daily for 7 days
Erythromycin 500 mg four times daily for 7 days
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Chlamydia.answer: Doxycycline 100 mg twice daily for 7 days
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Chlamydia.explanation: First-line for uncomplicated chlamydia is doxycycline 100 mg BD for 7 days. Single-dose azithromycin has been removed as a routine option because doxycycline has higher cure rates (especially rectal infection and against Mycoplasma genitalium). Ceftriaxone is for gonorrhoea; penicillin is for syphilis.

conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Chlamydia.question: A pregnant woman at 12 weeks tests positive for uncomplicated genital chlamydia. What is the most appropriate treatment and follow-up?
options: Doxycycline 100 mg BD for 7 days, no test of cure
Azithromycin 1 g then 500 mg OD for 2 days (or erythromycin), with a test of cure
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Chlamydia.answer: Azithromycin 1 g then 500 mg OD for 2 days (or erythromycin), with a test of cure
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Chlamydia.explanation: Doxycycline is contraindicated in pregnancy, so the regimen is azithromycin 1 g stat then 500 mg OD for 2 days (or erythromycin 500 mg QDS for 7 days). A test of cure IS recommended in pregnancy (done ≥3–5 weeks after treatment). Untreated chlamydia risks preterm birth, PROM and neonatal conjunctivitis/pneumonia.

conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Chlamydia.question: A 20-year-old woman treated for chlamydia asks when she can have sex again. What is the correct advice?
options: After 7 days and once all partners have completed treatment
After a negative test of cure at 1 week
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Chlamydia.answer: After 7 days and once all partners have completed treatment
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Chlamydia.explanation: Advise no sex for 7 days after starting treatment AND until all partners have completed treatment, to avoid reinfection. Referral to GUM for contact tracing (look back ~6 months or to the last partner) and testing for other STIs are also part of management.

conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Chlamydia.question: An MSM patient presents with a change in bowel habit, anal pain, tenesmus and rectal discharge, and is found to have a rectal chlamydia NAAT positive for an L-serovar. What is the diagnosis and the correct treatment?
options: Uncomplicated chlamydia — doxycycline 100 mg BD for 7 days
Lymphogranuloma venereum — doxycycline 100 mg BD for 21 days
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Chlamydia.answer: Lymphogranuloma venereum — doxycycline 100 mg BD for 21 days
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Chlamydia.explanation: Serovars L1–L3 cause lymphogranuloma venereum, which in MSM classically presents with proctocolitis (can mimic IBD). LGV requires a longer course: doxycycline 100 mg BD for 21 days (vs 7 days for uncomplicated chlamydia). HIV co-infection is common and should be tested for.

conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Chlamydia.question: A woman is treated for chlamydia. Regarding a repeat NAAT test, which statement is correct?
options: A test of cure is routinely required for all patients at 1 week
A test of cure is not routine but is recommended in pregnancy, rectal infection or persistent symptoms, done at ≥3–5 weeks
A repeat test at 3 months is a test of cure
NAAT should be repeated at 48 hours to confirm eradication
No repeat testing is ever needed after treatment
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Chlamydia.answer: A test of cure is not routine but is recommended in pregnancy, rectal infection or persistent symptoms, done at ≥3–5 weeks
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Chlamydia.explanation: A test of cure is not routine (treatment is highly effective) but is recommended in pregnancy, for rectal infection, or if symptoms persist — and must be delayed to ≥3–5 weeks because NAAT can remain positive from dead organisms. The separate 3-month re-test detects reinfection, not cure.

conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Chlamydia.question: A 19-year-old man develops bilateral conjunctivitis, dysuria and an acutely swollen painful knee two weeks after an episode of urethritis. What is the most likely underlying trigger?
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Chlamydia.explanation: The triad of conjunctivitis, urethritis and arthritis ('can't see, can't pee, can't climb a tree') is reactive arthritis, classically triggered by chlamydia. It is a sterile, post-infectious arthritis rather than direct joint infection, so the joint fluid is not purulent with organisms.

conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Chlamydia.question: Which is the correct first-line NAAT specimen for detecting genital chlamydia in a woman and in a man respectively?
options: Endocervical swab in women; urethral swab in men
Vulvovaginal swab in women; first-catch urine in men
First-catch urine in women; vulvovaginal swab in men
High vaginal swab in women; mid-stream urine in men
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Chlamydia.answer: Vulvovaginal swab in women; first-catch urine in men
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Chlamydia.explanation: NAAT is the diagnostic test. The first-line specimens are a vulvovaginal swab in women (self-taken is acceptable and as sensitive) and a first-catch urine in men. Additional rectal/pharyngeal swabs are taken according to exposure.

conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Chlamydia.question: A woman with chlamydial PID develops right upper quadrant pain. Perihepatitis is suspected. What is this complication called?
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Chlamydia.explanation: Fitz-Hugh-Curtis syndrome is perihepatitis (inflammation of the liver capsule with 'violin-string' adhesions) complicating chlamydial (or gonococcal) PID, causing RUQ pain. It is a classic examinable complication of ascending genital chlamydia.

conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Chlamydia.question: A baby born vaginally to a mother with untreated chlamydia develops a purulent conjunctivitis at 7 days of age. What is the most likely cause and an associated systemic complication?
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Chlamydia.explanation: Vertical transmission of chlamydia causes neonatal conjunctivitis (ophthalmia neonatorum), typically presenting around 5–14 days, and can also cause chlamydial pneumonia. (Gonococcal ophthalmia tends to present earlier, in the first few days.)

conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Chlamydia.question: A sexually active 24-year-old woman is diagnosed with chlamydia. She reports oral and anal sex with her partner. What is the most appropriate testing approach?
options: Test at all sites of potential exposure — vulvovaginal, plus rectal and pharyngeal swabs — and offer a full STI screen
A blood test for chlamydia antibodies
Test only if she develops symptoms at those sites
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Chlamydia.answer: Test at all sites of potential exposure — vulvovaginal, plus rectal and pharyngeal swabs — and offer a full STI screen
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Chlamydia.explanation: Chlamydia should be tested at all sites of potential exposure: vulvovaginal swab plus rectal (anal sex) and pharyngeal (oral sex) swabs. A full STI screen (gonorrhoea, syphilis, HIV) should also be offered, as coinfection is common.

conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Chlamydia.question: Regarding the 3-month re-test recommended after a positive chlamydia result, what is its purpose?
options: To confirm the original treatment cured the infection
To detect reinfection, as young positive patients are at high risk of a new infection
To confirm the NAAT has become negative
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Chlamydia.answer: To detect reinfection, as young positive patients are at high risk of a new infection
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Chlamydia.explanation: The 3-month re-test after a positive result is designed to detect reinfection (common in this high-risk group), NOT to confirm cure — treatment is highly effective, so a test of cure is not routinely needed. Any test of cure, when indicated, is done separately at ≥3–5 weeks.

conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Chlamydia.question: A 22-year-old man with a penicillin allergy and no other issues is diagnosed with uncomplicated urethral chlamydia. What is the most appropriate treatment?
options: He cannot be treated because of the penicillin allergy
Doxycycline 100 mg twice daily for 7 days — penicillin allergy is not relevant
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Chlamydia.answer: Doxycycline 100 mg twice daily for 7 days — penicillin allergy is not relevant
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Chlamydia.explanation: Chlamydia is treated with doxycycline, which is unrelated to penicillin, so a penicillin allergy is irrelevant. First-line remains doxycycline 100 mg BD for 7 days. (Penicillins are not used for chlamydia at all.)

conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Chlamydia.question: Which statement about the presentation of chlamydia is most accurate?
options: It is symptomatic in almost all infected people
It is asymptomatic in around 70% of women and 50% of men, which is the rationale for screening
It always causes a purulent urethral discharge
Symptoms reliably appear within 24 hours of exposure
Women are always symptomatic while men are not
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Chlamydia.answer: It is asymptomatic in around 70% of women and 50% of men, which is the rationale for screening
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Chlamydia.explanation: Most chlamydia infections are asymptomatic (~70% of women, ~50% of men), so infection spreads silently. This asymptomatic majority is precisely why an opportunistic national screening programme for under-25s exists rather than relying on symptomatic presentation.

conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Chlamydia.question: A patient with confirmed genital chlamydia is also found to have gonorrhoea on the same STI screen. Which principle does this illustrate about chlamydia management?
options: Chlamydia never coexists with other STIs
Coinfection is common, so a full STI screen (gonorrhoea, syphilis, HIV) and GUM referral for contact tracing should be routine
Only chlamydia needs treating in coinfection
Screening for other STIs is unnecessary once chlamydia is found
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Chlamydia.answer: Coinfection is common, so a full STI screen (gonorrhoea, syphilis, HIV) and GUM referral for contact tracing should be routine
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Chlamydia.explanation: Finding chlamydia should always prompt a full STI screen because coinfection (e.g. with gonorrhoea) is common, and GUM referral for partner notification/contact tracing is standard. Both infections are then treated according to their own regimens.

conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Chlamydia.question: A woman treated for chlamydia with doxycycline reports she is now 5 weeks pregnant and was treated at 2 weeks' gestation before she knew. What is the most appropriate action?
options: Terminate the pregnancy due to doxycycline exposure
Reassure, arrange a test of cure (recommended in pregnancy), and note the exposure was very early with low risk
Immediately repeat a full 21-day doxycycline course
Start a prophylactic azithromycin course indefinitely
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Chlamydia.answer: Reassure, arrange a test of cure (recommended in pregnancy), and note the exposure was very early with low risk
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Chlamydia.explanation: A test of cure is recommended in pregnancy, so that should be arranged (≥3–5 weeks post-treatment). Very early inadvertent doxycycline exposure carries low risk and does not warrant termination; the tetracycline concern (dental/skeletal) relates to use in the second/third trimester. Reassurance and appropriate follow-up are correct.

conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Chlamydia.question: What is the characteristic feature of the PRIMARY stage of lymphogranuloma venereum?
options: A painful genital ulcer with a hard base
A small, transient, painless genital or rectal ulcer/papule
A widespread maculopapular rash on palms and soles
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Chlamydia.answer: A small, transient, painless genital or rectal ulcer/papule
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Chlamydia.explanation: Primary LGV is a small, transient, PAINLESS genital/rectal ulcer or papule that is easily missed. Painful inguinal lymphadenopathy ('buboes') is the secondary stage, and proctocolitis is the tertiary stage. (A painless ulcer also features in primary syphilis — context and NAAT distinguish them.)

conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Chlamydia.question: A 23-year-old woman with symptomatic chlamydia has cervical motion tenderness, adnexal tenderness and fever, suggesting pelvic inflammatory disease. Compared with uncomplicated chlamydia, how does this change management priorities?
options: Treat with the standard 7-day doxycycline for uncomplicated chlamydia only
She needs broader empirical PID treatment covering chlamydia, gonorrhoea and anaerobes, not just single-agent chlamydia therapy
No antibiotics are needed as PID is viral
She should have a test of cure before any treatment
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Chlamydia.answer: She needs broader empirical PID treatment covering chlamydia, gonorrhoea and anaerobes, not just single-agent chlamydia therapy
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Chlamydia.explanation: Signs of PID (cervical motion tenderness, adnexal tenderness, fever) indicate ascending infection requiring broader empirical antibiotic cover for chlamydia, gonorrhoea and anaerobes (e.g. ceftriaxone + doxycycline + metronidazole), started before results, rather than single-agent chlamydia treatment — to protect fertility and prevent ectopic/chronic pain.

conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Candidiasis (.question: A 28-year-old woman presents with intense vulval itch and a thick, white, 'cottage cheese' discharge with no offensive odour. Vaginal pH is 4.0. What is the most likely diagnosis?
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Candidiasis (.explanation: Intense vulval itch, thick white non-offensive 'cottage cheese' discharge and a normal pH <4.5 are classic for vulvovaginal candidiasis. BV and trichomonas both raise the pH >4.5; the normal pH plus prominent itch is the cleanest discriminator pointing to thrush.

conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Candidiasis (.question: A 25-year-old non-pregnant woman with typical, uncomplicated vaginal thrush attends. What is the most appropriate first-line management?
options: Send a high vaginal swab and await results before treating
Oral metronidazole 400 mg BD for 7 days
Treat her sexual partner as well
A 2 g single dose of metronidazole
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Candidiasis (.explanation: For uncomplicated candidiasis in a non-pregnant woman, first-line is single-dose oral fluconazole 150 mg. A swab is not routinely needed when the picture is typical. Metronidazole treats BV/trichomonas, not candida, and partners are not treated as it is not an STI.

conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Candidiasis (.question: A pregnant woman at 24 weeks has symptomatic vaginal candidiasis. What is the most appropriate treatment?
options: An intravaginal azole (clotrimazole) pessary/cream, often for a longer course
No treatment as it resolves spontaneously
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Candidiasis (.answer: An intravaginal azole (clotrimazole) pessary/cream, often for a longer course
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Candidiasis (.explanation: Oral fluconazole is avoided in pregnancy because of the risk of congenital abnormalities. Treatment is topical only — an intravaginal azole (clotrimazole) pessary/cream, often a longer course (up to 7 days). Metronidazole treats BV/trichomonas, not candida.

conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Candidiasis (.question: A 34-year-old woman has had 5 symptomatic episodes of candidiasis this year. Besides confirming the diagnosis with a swab, which investigation is most important to exclude an underlying cause?
options: Blood glucose / HbA1c to exclude diabetes
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Candidiasis (.answer: Blood glucose / HbA1c to exclude diabetes
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Candidiasis (.explanation: Recurrent candidiasis (≥4 episodes/year) warrants a search for an underlying cause — most importantly diabetes, so check blood glucose/HbA1c. A confirmatory HVS for MCS (species/resistance) and exclusion of differentials such as lichen sclerosus are also part of the workup.

conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Candidiasis (.question: Which of the following is the most appropriate induction–maintenance regimen for recurrent vulvovaginal candidiasis?
options: Induction: fluconazole every 3 days for 3 doses; maintenance: fluconazole 150 mg weekly for 6 months
Topical clotrimazole once and treat the partner
Continuous daily oral fluconazole for 2 years
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Candidiasis (.answer: Induction: fluconazole every 3 days for 3 doses; maintenance: fluconazole 150 mg weekly for 6 months
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Candidiasis (.explanation: Recurrent candidiasis is managed with an induction–maintenance regimen: induction with oral fluconazole every 3 days for 3 doses (days 1, 4, 7), then maintenance with oral fluconazole 150 mg weekly for 6 months, after confirming the diagnosis and excluding diabetes/differentials.

conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Candidiasis (.question: A woman recently completed a course of broad-spectrum antibiotics for a chest infection and now has vulval itch with a thick white discharge. What best explains her symptoms?
options: The antibiotics directly caused a yeast mutation
The antibiotics wiped out protective vaginal bacteria, allowing Candida overgrowth
She has acquired a sexually transmitted infection
The antibiotics raised her vaginal pH above 4.5
This is an allergic reaction to the antibiotic
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Candidiasis (.answer: The antibiotics wiped out protective vaginal bacteria, allowing Candida overgrowth
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Candidiasis (.explanation: Broad-spectrum antibiotics disturb the normal vaginal flora by eliminating protective lactobacilli, allowing colonising Candida to overgrow and cause symptomatic thrush. This is a classic predisposing factor, alongside diabetes, pregnancy, immunosuppression and high-oestrogen states.

conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Candidiasis (.question: A woman with a woman partner is diagnosed with vaginal candidiasis and asks whether her partner needs treatment. What is the correct advice?
options: Yes — both partners must be treated to prevent reinfection
No — candidiasis is not sexually transmitted, so partners are not treated
Only if the partner has symptoms of thrush
The partner needs a full STI screen and treatment
Both must abstain from sex for a month
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Candidiasis (.answer: No — candidiasis is not sexually transmitted, so partners are not treated
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Candidiasis (.explanation: Candidiasis is not sexually transmitted, so routine partner treatment is not recommended (unlike true STIs such as trichomonas/chlamydia/gonorrhoea). Treatment is directed at the symptomatic individual.

conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Candidiasis (.question: A woman with suspected typical thrush is worried a swab has not been taken. What is the correct explanation regarding investigations?
options: A high vaginal swab is mandatory in all cases before treatment
If the picture is typical, diagnose clinically and treat; a swab is reserved for recurrent, atypical or treatment-failure cases
A cervical smear is the definitive diagnostic test
Blood cultures are needed to confirm candida
A swab must be sent to check her partner is not the source
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Candidiasis (.answer: If the picture is typical, diagnose clinically and treat; a swab is reserved for recurrent, atypical or treatment-failure cases
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Candidiasis (.explanation: Uncomplicated thrush with a typical picture is a clinical diagnosis and can be treated without a swab. HVS for microscopy/culture is reserved for recurrent, atypical or treatment-failure cases (e.g. to identify non-albicans species like C. glabrata). A smear is not the diagnostic test.

conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Candidiasis (.question: A woman with recurrent thrush is not responding to standard fluconazole. An HVS grows a non-albicans species. Which organism is most likely and why does it matter?
options: Candida glabrata — it may be azole-resistant, explaining treatment failure
Gardnerella vaginalis — it causes BV not thrush
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Candidiasis (.answer: Candida glabrata — it may be azole-resistant, explaining treatment failure
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Candidiasis (.explanation: Most candidiasis is Candida albicans, but recurrent or treatment-failure cases may be due to non-albicans species such as Candida glabrata, which can be less sensitive to azoles — hence the value of an HVS for species identification and sensitivities in these cases.

conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Candidiasis (.question: A woman with vulvovaginal candidiasis has prominent vulval itching and erythema in addition to vaginal symptoms. Alongside oral fluconazole, what should be added?
options: A topical imidazole (clotrimazole) cream applied to the vulva
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Candidiasis (.answer: A topical imidazole (clotrimazole) cream applied to the vulva
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Candidiasis (.explanation: When there are vulval symptoms, a topical imidazole cream (e.g. clotrimazole) to the vulva is added to relieve the external vulvitis, alongside the oral or intravaginal antifungal. Oral and topical azoles have similar cure rates, so choice is often patient preference.

conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Candidiasis (.question: Which statement about vaginal pH in the discharge differential is correct?
options: Candida raises the pH above 4.5 like BV
Candida has a normal pH below 4.5, whereas BV and trichomonas both raise it above 4.5
All three conditions have a pH below 4.5
Trichomonas has a normal pH below 4.5
pH is not helpful in distinguishing these conditions
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Candidiasis (.answer: Candida has a normal pH below 4.5, whereas BV and trichomonas both raise it above 4.5
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Candidiasis (.explanation: Vaginal pH is the key bedside discriminator: candida keeps a normal pH <4.5, whereas both bacterial vaginosis and trichomoniasis raise the pH above 4.5. This, combined with the itch and discharge character, rapidly triages the discharge differential.

conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Candidiasis (.question: A woman using latex condoms is prescribed a topical azole pessary for thrush. What practical advice is important?
options: Some topical azoles can damage latex condoms and diaphragms, reducing their reliability
She should double up on condoms during treatment
Topical azoles have no effect on contraception
She must stop all contraception during treatment
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Candidiasis (.answer: Some topical azoles can damage latex condoms and diaphragms, reducing their reliability
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Candidiasis (.explanation: Some topical azole preparations can damage latex condoms and diaphragms, so women should be warned that these barrier methods may be less reliable during treatment and additional precautions considered. Avoiding vaginal irritants (soaps, douching) is also advised.

conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Candidiasis (.question: A poorly controlled diabetic woman presents with her third episode of thrush in 6 months. Which factor is most directly responsible for her recurrent candidiasis?
options: Poorly controlled diabetes (hyperglycaemia favours candida growth)
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Candidiasis (.answer: Poorly controlled diabetes (hyperglycaemia favours candida growth)
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Candidiasis (.explanation: Poorly controlled diabetes is a classic predisposing factor for recurrent candidiasis, as elevated glucose favours yeast growth and impairs local defences. Optimising glycaemic control is an important part of managing recurrent thrush, alongside the induction–maintenance antifungal regimen.

conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Candidiasis (.question: Which of the following correctly summarises the management contrast between candidiasis and bacterial vaginosis regarding partners?
options: Neither candidiasis nor BV requires partner treatment, as neither is an STI
Candidiasis requires partner treatment but BV does not
BV requires partner treatment but candidiasis does not
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Candidiasis (.answer: Neither candidiasis nor BV requires partner treatment, as neither is an STI
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Candidiasis (.explanation: Neither candidiasis nor bacterial vaginosis is a sexually transmitted infection, so neither requires partner treatment. This contrasts with trichomoniasis, chlamydia and gonorrhoea, which are STIs requiring partner notification/treatment.

conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Candidiasis (.question: A woman presents with vulval itch, but examination shows well-demarcated white atrophic patches and figure-of-eight perianal involvement rather than typical thrush, and repeated antifungals have not helped. What alternative diagnosis should be considered?
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Candidiasis (.explanation: Persistent vulval itch not responding to antifungals, with white atrophic/porcelain patches and a figure-of-eight perianal distribution, suggests lichen sclerosus rather than candidiasis. Excluding differentials such as lichen sclerosus and dermatitis is an explicit part of the recurrent-candidiasis workup.

conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Bacterial Vag.question: A 24-year-old woman attends the GUM clinic with a thin, grey, fishy-smelling discharge after a new sexual partner. Vaginal pH is 5.0, there is no itch, and clue cells are seen on microscopy. What is the most important initial step alongside making the diagnosis?
options: Treat her male partner with metronidazole
Offer a full STI screen, as BV is a marker of sexual-risk exposure and co-exists with STIs
Reassure her and give no treatment
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Bacterial Vag.answer: Offer a full STI screen, as BV is a marker of sexual-risk exposure and co-exists with STIs
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Bacterial Vag.explanation: This is BV (thin grey fishy discharge, pH >4.5, clue cells, no itch). In GUM, BV is not an STI but is a flag of sexual-risk exposure and frequently co-exists with STIs, so a full STI screen (chlamydia/gonorrhoea NAAT, trichomonas, HIV, syphilis) should be offered. Male partners are NOT treated.

conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Bacterial Vag.question: A woman is diagnosed with bacterial vaginosis in a sexual health clinic. She asks whether her male partner needs treatment. What is the correct advice?
options: Yes — he must take metronidazole to prevent recurrence
No — partner treatment does not reduce recurrence and is not recommended for BV
He needs a full course of doxycycline
He should be contact-traced like a chlamydia contact
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Bacterial Vag.answer: No — partner treatment does not reduce recurrence and is not recommended for BV
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Bacterial Vag.explanation: BV is not sexually transmitted, and treating male partners does not reduce recurrence, so partner treatment is not recommended — a key contrast with true STIs such as trichomoniasis, chlamydia and gonorrhoea, which do require partner notification/treatment.

conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Bacterial Vag.question: In a GUM clinic, which feature best distinguishes bacterial vaginosis from trichomoniasis, given both can raise vaginal pH and smell fishy?
options: BV causes a frothy yellow-green discharge
Trichomoniasis is an STI requiring partner notification, whereas BV is not
Only BV causes intense vulval itch
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Bacterial Vag.answer: Trichomoniasis is an STI requiring partner notification, whereas BV is not
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Bacterial Vag.explanation: BV and trichomoniasis can look similar (both raise pH >4.5 and can smell fishy), but trichomoniasis is a true STI that triggers partner notification/contact tracing, whereas BV is sexually associated but not an STI and needs no partner treatment. Trichomonas classically gives a frothy green discharge with itch.

conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Bacterial Vag.question: A woman with confirmed BV is prescribed oral metronidazole. Which piece of advice is essential?
options: Take it with a glass of wine to reduce nausea
Avoid alcohol during and just after the course (disulfiram-like reaction)
Use vaginal douching daily to clear the infection
Stop the course as soon as symptoms improve
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Bacterial Vag.answer: Avoid alcohol during and just after the course (disulfiram-like reaction)
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Bacterial Vag.explanation: Metronidazole causes a disulfiram-like reaction with alcohol (flushing, vomiting), so alcohol must be avoided. Douching should be discouraged as it disturbs the flora and predisposes to recurrence; the full course should be completed.

conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Bacterial Vag.question: Which set of findings satisfies Amsel's criteria for diagnosing bacterial vaginosis?
options: Thick curdy discharge, pH 4.0, hyphae on microscopy, negative whiff
Thin white homogenous discharge, pH 5.0, clue cells, positive whiff test
Frothy green discharge, pH 6.0, motile trophozoites, cervical friability
Mucopurulent discharge, pH 4.2, polymorphs, positive NAAT
Bloody discharge, pH 5.5, atypical cells, negative whiff
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Bacterial Vag.answer: Thin white homogenous discharge, pH 5.0, clue cells, positive whiff test
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Bacterial Vag.explanation: Amsel's criteria (≥3 of 4): thin white homogenous discharge, vaginal pH >4.5, clue cells on microscopy, and a positive whiff/amine test. The second option meets all four. Hyphae suggest candida; motile trophozoites suggest trichomonas.

conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Bacterial Vag.question: A pregnant woman at 20 weeks has symptomatic bacterial vaginosis. What is the most appropriate management?
options: No treatment is ever given in pregnancy
Treat with oral metronidazole, avoiding the high-dose single 2 g regimen
Treat only with a single 2 g metronidazole dose
Treat her partner and observe her
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Bacterial Vag.answer: Treat with oral metronidazole, avoiding the high-dose single 2 g regimen
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Bacterial Vag.explanation: Symptomatic BV in pregnancy should be treated because it is linked to preterm birth, miscarriage, PROM, chorioamnionitis, low birth weight and postpartum endometritis. Oral metronidazole is used, avoiding the high-dose single 2 g regimen. Fluconazole treats candida, not BV.

conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Bacterial Vag.question: A woman asks why her recurrent BV keeps coming back despite treatment. Which factor should be specifically addressed as a modifiable cause?
options: Vaginal douching and use of vaginal soaps/shower gels
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Bacterial Vag.answer: Vaginal douching and use of vaginal soaps/shower gels
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Bacterial Vag.explanation: Douching and use of vaginal soaps/shower gels disturb the protective lactobacilli and predispose to recurrence, so avoiding them is the key preventive advice. Recurrence is common (~50–70% within a year); modifiable factors should be addressed and suppressive regimens considered for frequent recurrence.

conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Bacterial Vag.question: Why is bacterial vaginosis clinically significant in the context of HIV, from a sexual health perspective?
options: It cures HIV by raising vaginal pH
It increases susceptibility to acquiring HIV/other STIs and increases onward HIV transmission
It has no relationship to HIV
It only matters if the woman is already HIV positive
It reduces the risk of acquiring STIs
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Bacterial Vag.answer: It increases susceptibility to acquiring HIV/other STIs and increases onward HIV transmission
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Bacterial Vag.explanation: The raised vaginal pH and loss of the lactobacillus barrier in BV increase susceptibility to acquiring STIs including HIV, and also increase onward HIV transmission risk — a major reason BV is taken seriously in sexual health and prompts full STI screening.

conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Bacterial Vag.question: A woman is found to have asymptomatic bacterial vaginosis on a routine GUM swab. She is not pregnant and has no planned procedures. What is the most appropriate management?
options: A 2 g single dose of metronidazole
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Bacterial Vag.explanation: Asymptomatic BV usually needs no treatment, except before a procedure (e.g. TOP, IUD insertion) or in pregnancy with risk factors. Reassurance and preventive advice (avoid douching/soaps) are appropriate here.

conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Bacterial Vag.question: A woman who has sex with women is diagnosed with BV and asks about her female partner. What is the correct advice?
options: Her partner must be treated with metronidazole
BV is more concordant between female partners — assessment can be considered, but routine partner treatment is still not recommended
Her partner needs contact tracing like a chlamydia contact
Female partners never need any consideration
Both must abstain from sex for 3 months
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Bacterial Vag.answer: BV is more concordant between female partners — assessment can be considered, but routine partner treatment is still not recommended
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Bacterial Vag.explanation: BV shows higher concordance in women who have sex with women, so assessment of a female partner can be considered. However, routine partner treatment is still not recommended for BV (there is no good evidence it reduces recurrence).

conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Bacterial Vag.question: A GUM clinician wants a rapid point-of-care assessment for a woman with suspected BV. Which combination is most appropriate?
options: Narrow-range vaginal pH paper plus microscopy of a wet/Gram-stained slide
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Bacterial Vag.answer: Narrow-range vaginal pH paper plus microscopy of a wet/Gram-stained slide
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Bacterial Vag.explanation: BV is diagnosed at the point of care using narrow-range pH paper (pH >4.5) plus microscopy of a wet or Gram-stained slide (clue cells; Hay-Ison/Nugent grading is the lab equivalent). This allows immediate diagnosis and the STI/not-STI triage that defines GUM management.

conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Bacterial Vag.question: A woman with a thick, white, curdy discharge and intense vulval itch has a vaginal pH of 4.0. Which diagnosis is most likely and does it require partner treatment?
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Bacterial Vag.explanation: Thick white curdy discharge, intense itch and pH <4.5 indicate vulvovaginal candidiasis, which is not an STI and does not require partner treatment. BV and trichomonas both give pH >4.5; only trichomonas (an STI) needs partner treatment.

conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Bacterial Vag.question: A 27-year-old with recurrent BV has completed several standard courses. She has frequent symptomatic episodes. What is a reasonable next step for management of frequent recurrence?
options: Address modifiable factors and consider a suppressive metronidazole regimen
Prophylactic treatment of all sexual partners
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Bacterial Vag.answer: Address modifiable factors and consider a suppressive metronidazole regimen
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Bacterial Vag.explanation: For frequent recurrence, address modifiable factors (avoid douching/soaps) and consider a suppressive regimen (e.g. intermittent topical/oral metronidazole). Partner treatment is not effective, fluconazole treats candida, and surgery is inappropriate.

conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Bacterial Vag.question: Which statement about the underlying microbiology of bacterial vaginosis is correct?
options: It results from overgrowth of lactobacilli lowering the pH
It results from loss of lactobacilli, a rise in pH above 4.5, and overgrowth of anaerobes such as Gardnerella vaginalis
It is caused by Candida albicans overgrowth
It is caused by the protozoan Trichomonas vaginalis
It is caused by Neisseria gonorrhoeae
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Bacterial Vag.answer: It results from loss of lactobacilli, a rise in pH above 4.5, and overgrowth of anaerobes such as Gardnerella vaginalis
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__Bacterial Vag.explanation: BV arises from loss of protective lactobacilli, allowing the vaginal pH to rise above 4.5 and anaerobes (chiefly Gardnerella vaginalis) to overgrow. It is not caused by candida, trichomonas or gonorrhoea — distinguishing it from those diagnoses is the core GUM skill.

conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__HPV / Genital.question: A 24-year-old man presents with several soft, non-keratinised painless lumps around the base of the penis. He would prefer to treat them at home. What is the most appropriate first-line treatment?
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__HPV / Genital.explanation: Multiple SOFT (non-keratinised) warts, especially with a preference for home treatment, are best treated first-line with patient-applied topical PODOPHYLLOTOXIN. Cryotherapy suits solitary keratinised warts and is clinician-applied; aciclovir treats HSV, not warts; TCA and surgery are second-line/for resistant disease.

conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__HPV / Genital.question: A 30-year-old woman has a single firm, keratinised painless wart on the perianal skin. Which first-line treatment is most appropriate?
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__HPV / Genital.explanation: A solitary KERATINISED (hard) wart is best treated with clinician-applied CRYOTHERAPY. Podophyllotoxin works best on soft warts; imiquimod is second-line; valaciclovir is for HSV. Treatment can be offered even though warts are benign, as they are often distressing.

conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__HPV / Genital.question: A 27-year-old woman who is 20 weeks pregnant has extensive genital warts. Which treatment is safe to use?
options: No treatment is permitted in pregnancy
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__HPV / Genital.explanation: In pregnancy, podophyllotoxin and imiquimod are CONTRAINDICATED; CRYOTHERAPY is the safe option. Treatment may be offered to reduce wart burden; there is a rare risk of neonatal laryngeal (recurrent respiratory) papillomatosis from vertical transmission.

conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__HPV / Genital.question: A patient is told their genital warts are caused by HPV. Which HPV types are responsible for around 90% of genital warts?
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__HPV / Genital.explanation: Low-risk HPV 6 and 11 cause about 90% of genital warts and do not cause cancer. HPV 16 and 18 are high-risk types causing ~70% of cervical cancer but do not typically cause warts. HPV 1 and 2 cause common skin (verruca) warts.

conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__HPV / Genital.question: A distressed 22-year-old with newly diagnosed genital warts asks whether his recent sexual partners must be contacted and treated. What is the correct advice?
options: Formal partner notification is mandatory, as for chlamydia
Contact tracing is not required, but partners may be assessed if they wish
All partners from the last 6 months must be treated empirically
The patient must abstain until all partners are traced
Partners require HPV testing before any sexual contact
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__HPV / Genital.answer: Contact tracing is not required, but partners may be assessed if they wish
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__HPV / Genital.explanation: Unlike bacterial STIs, genital warts do NOT require contact tracing/partner notification. Partners can be seen if they wish (e.g. for assessment or an STI screen), but there is no mandatory notification, empirical partner treatment, or partner HPV testing requirement.

conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__HPV / Genital.question: A 19-year-old woman treated successfully for genital warts asks about the chance they will come back. What is the most accurate counselling?
options: Recurrence is almost never seen after clearance
Recurrence occurs in about 30% and warts may return after apparent clearance
Recurrence means the treatment has failed and antivirals are needed
Recurrence only happens if she acquires a new infection
Recurrence indicates progression to cervical cancer
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__HPV / Genital.answer: Recurrence occurs in about 30% and warts may return after apparent clearance
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__HPV / Genital.explanation: Recurrence is common (~30%) even after apparent clearance, because HPV can persist in clinically normal skin; patients should be warned. It does not signify treatment failure requiring antivirals, a definite new infection, or progression to cancer (warts are caused by low-risk types).

conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__HPV / Genital.question: A 25-year-old man has extensive keratinised genital warts that have not responded to two courses of podophyllotoxin. Which second-line option is most appropriate and has a lower recurrence rate?
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__HPV / Genital.explanation: For larger/keratinised warts or first-line failure, topical IMIQUIMOD (an immune-response modifier) is an appropriate second-line agent and has a LOWER recurrence rate than podophyllotoxin. Aciclovir treats HSV; corticosteroids have no role; simply repeating a failed agent is not best practice.

conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__HPV / Genital.question: A parent asks what the HPV vaccine given at school protects against. Which statement about Gardasil 9 (the current UK vaccine) is correct?
options: It covers only the cancer-causing types 16 and 18
It covers types 6, 11, 16 and 18 plus five other high-risk types, preventing warts and cancers
It only prevents genital warts, not cancer
It replaces the need for cervical screening
It is offered only to girls
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__HPV / Genital.answer: It covers types 6, 11, 16 and 18 plus five other high-risk types, preventing warts and cancers
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__HPV / Genital.explanation: Gardasil 9 covers low-risk 6 and 11 (warts) and high-risk 16 and 18 plus five further high-risk types (31, 33, 45, 52, 58), preventing both warts and HPV-related cancers/pre-cancers. It is offered to both sexes, and cervical screening should still continue.

conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__HPV / Genital.question: Under the current UK programme, when and how is the routine HPV vaccine given to adolescents?
options: Year 8, both boys and girls, as a single dose
Girls only, in Year 8, three doses
At birth as part of the neonatal schedule
Only to those who are already sexually active
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__HPV / Genital.answer: Year 8, both boys and girls, as a single dose
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__HPV / Genital.explanation: Since September 2023 the routine adolescent HPV vaccine is a SINGLE DOSE, offered to both boys and girls in school Year 8 (age 12-13), given before sexual debut for maximum benefit. MSM up to 45 and other at-risk groups are also eligible via specialist services.

conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__HPV / Genital.question: A 23-year-old woman who received the HPV vaccine at school asks whether she still needs cervical screening. What is the best advice?
options: No, the vaccine gives complete protection
Yes, she should continue cervical screening as recommended
Screening is only needed if she develops warts
She should be screened annually because she was vaccinated
Screening is unnecessary unless she is symptomatic
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__HPV / Genital.answer: Yes, she should continue cervical screening as recommended
conditions__SEXUAL HEALTH__HPV / Genital.explanation: Vaccination does not cover every high-risk HPV type or clear pre-existing infection, so vaccinated women should still attend routine cervical screening. Screening intervals follow the national programme (not annual), and are not contingent on symptoms or warts.
